text.p: Singleton Group Ltd said it had sold its 10 percent voting stake in television network TEN Group Ltd for A$59.15 million to a company associated with Melbourne businessman Isi Leibler, who already has a five percent stake.
Singleton said the 4.555 million TEN shares were sold for A$13 each compared with the original purchase price of A$4.550 million in December 1992.
The TEN stake was sold to Leibler Media Holdings Pty Ltd, and a nominee for CanWest companies, Selli Pty Ltd. Corporate sources told Reuters that Selli provided the financing.
Liebler was not available for comment while a spokesman for the local office of CanWest said he could not comment.
The Singleton stake values TEN, the third-ranked network in Australia, at A$1.18 billion based on Singleton's five percent economic interest.

CanWest Global Communications Corp (CanWest) has a 15 percent voting interest and a 57.5 percent economic interest in TEN. The voting interest is the maximum allowable under national foreign investment and industry regulations.
The Singleton sale occurred under a pre-emptive rights deal with other TEN shareholders.
